Name: Requirements Gathering
Key Signals: Asks clarifying questions before designing; identifies functional and non-functional requirements; scopes the problem
Common Mistakes: Jumps straight to solution without understanding requirements; doesn't ask about scale or constraints; over-scopes
Evaluation Criteria: Did the candidate ask about: users/scale; read vs write heavy; latency requirements; consistency needs; budget/timeline?

Name: Back-of-Envelope Estimation
Key Signals: Estimates QPS from DAU; calculates storage and bandwidth; identifies bottlenecks with numbers
Common Mistakes: Uses round numbers without justification; forgets peak vs average; ignores replication/overhead
Evaluation Criteria: Are calculations reasonable? Does candidate use numbers to drive design decisions? Little's Law for concurrency?

Name: High-Level Architecture
Key Signals: Draws clear component diagram; identifies data flow; separates read and write paths; names technologies with justification
Common Mistakes: Draws boxes without explaining data flow; picks technologies without justification; single point of failure in design
Evaluation Criteria: Is the architecture complete? Are component responsibilities clear? Are choices justified with trade-offs?

Name: Database Schema Design
Key Signals: Designs schema that supports query patterns; considers denormalization trade-offs; identifies indexes
Common Mistakes: Normalizes excessively for a read-heavy system; forgets about query patterns; no index planning
Evaluation Criteria: Does schema support the identified query patterns? Are hot paths optimized? Is denormalization justified?

Name: API Design
Key Signals: Designs clean RESTful or RPC APIs with proper resource naming; considers pagination and error handling and versioning
Common Mistakes: Inconsistent naming; no pagination for list endpoints; no error response format; forgets authentication
Evaluation Criteria: Are APIs intuitive? Is pagination included? Are error codes meaningful? Is backward compatibility considered?

Name: Scaling Discussion
Key Signals: Identifies bottlenecks and proposes horizontal scaling; discusses caching layers and CDN and read replicas and sharding
Common Mistakes: Only mentions vertical scaling; adds complexity without quantifying the need; doesn't discuss trade-offs of sharding
Evaluation Criteria: Does scaling approach match the estimated load? Are trade-offs articulated? Is incremental scaling considered?

Name: Trade-off Analysis
Key Signals: Explicitly names trade-offs for every major decision; considers 2-3 alternatives before choosing; articulates why-not
Common Mistakes: Presents one solution as obviously correct; doesn't consider alternatives; ignores operational complexity trade-offs
Evaluation Criteria: Does candidate say 'I chose X over Y because Z'? Are trade-offs quantified where possible?

Name: Failure Mode Analysis
Key Signals: Proactively identifies what can fail; designs for graceful degradation; discusses retry/timeout/circuit breaker strategies
Common Mistakes: Happy path only design; no mention of failure modes; doesn't discuss what happens when a dependency is down
Evaluation Criteria: Does candidate identify: network failures; service failures; data inconsistency; cascading failures? Are mitigations concrete?

Name: Consistency vs Availability
Key Signals: Articulates CAP/PACELC trade-offs for their specific system; chooses consistency model per data type not globally
Common Mistakes: Blanket 'everything is eventually consistent' or 'everything must be strongly consistent'; doesn't differentiate by data type
Evaluation Criteria: Does candidate choose different consistency models for different parts of the system? Are choices justified by user experience?

Name: Operational Concerns
Key Signals: Discusses monitoring and alerting and deployment strategy and runbooks; considers day-2 operations not just day-1 design
Common Mistakes: No mention of observability; no deployment strategy; doesn't discuss how to debug issues in production
Evaluation Criteria: Does candidate discuss: SLIs/SLOs; alerting strategy; deployment (canary/blue-green); on-call considerations?

Name: Cost Awareness
Key Signals: Considers infrastructure cost in design decisions; identifies expensive components; proposes cost optimization strategies
Common Mistakes: Designs without any cost consideration; uses the most expensive option for every component; ignores egress costs
Evaluation Criteria: Does candidate mention cost trade-offs? Are expensive components (cross-region; GPUs; managed services) justified?

Name: Communication and Structure
Key Signals: Structures answers clearly; uses STAR format for behavioral questions; communicates technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders
Common Mistakes: Rambling answers without structure; too much detail on irrelevant aspects; can't simplify for non-technical audience
Evaluation Criteria: Is the answer structured? Does candidate adapt communication to the audience? Do they signal when they're going deep?
